items.stem: A Bedrock assistant must answer strictly from approved company documents and show where each answer came from. Which approach fits best?

options.text: Ground answers with a knowledge base and return citations
options.rationale: Correct: a knowledge base supplies approved context and citations show provenance.

options.text: Raise the temperature to encourage creativity
options.rationale: Creativity increases the risk of unsupported answers.
Unapproved data undermines the 'approved documents only' requirement.

options.text: Remove all retrieval and rely on the base model
options.rationale: Without retrieval the assistant cannot cite approved sources.

items.explanation: Correct: a knowledge base supplies approved context and citations show provenance.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO practices follow least privilege for Bedrock access? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Grant only the specific Bedrock actions the caller needs
options.rationale: Correct: scoping actions limits what a principal can do.

options.text: Restrict access to the specific models in use
options.rationale: Correct: limiting model access reduces exposure.

options.text: Attach a policy allowing bedrock:* to every role
Share one admin key among all applications
options.rationale: Shared admin keys remove accountability and over-permit.

items.explanation: Correct: both keyed options are right; the distractors are wrong for the reasons given.

items.stem: Before launch, your team wants to compare answer quality across prompt changes objectively. What should you create first?

options.text: A labelled evaluation set scored with a rubric
options.rationale: Correct: a fixed, labelled set makes quality comparable across changes.
One prompt is not a reliable measure.
Token limits do not measure answer quality.

items.explanation: Correct: a fixed, labelled set makes quality comparable across changes.
